Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Maninder S. Bhatti

On The 12 th Of July, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 22790 of 2024
 Dinesh Rajak
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Ranjan Benerjee - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Sudeep Kumar Patel - Advocate for the objector.
Shri Vivek Lakhera - Government Advocate for the State.

Order 
This is the Second application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.354/2023 dated 04.10.2023 registered at Police Station Bameetha, District Chhatarpur for the offence punishable under Section 363, 376,
376(3), 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
Earlier bail application was dismissed on 23/01/2024 as withdrawn with liberty to revisit this Court after examination of the prosecutrix.

2 . It is contended by the counsel that after dismissal of earlier application, the case was fixed before the trial Court for as many as 8 to 9 occasions and the order-sheets have been brought on record as Annexure P/3 which reflects that prosecution witnesses are not turning up despite repeated summons issued by the trial Court.
Thus, the applicant who is aged about 21 years is in custody since 08/10/2023 deserves to be enlarged on bail as there is lax handiling at the instance of the prosecution.

4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as objector have 2 MCRC-22790-2024 opposed the prayer and submitted that there is a seizure of 28 bottles of Onrex Co d eine Phosphate Cough Syrup from the applicant and the previous application was withdrawn by the applicant inasmuch as there are direct allegation of commission of offence.
Therefore, taking into consideration the conduct of the applicant, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

5. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
6.

A perusal of the case diary it reflects that after dismissal of the previous application, the case was listed on as many as 9 occasion before the trial Court and the order-sheet reflects that the not only Dinesh Rajak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130892201/
1 the prosecution even other prosecution witnesses including the mother of the prosecutrix has not turned up as yet.

sentences.text: The applicant is aged about 21 years and is in custody since 08.10.2023.

7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, including the incarceration period already suffered by the applicant, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant- Dinesh Rajak shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction o f the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

9. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
10.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
